From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: quick TCO question after demo — Acme TCO recap

Hi Jordan / Priya — great talking earlier. Quick post-call recap focused on costs and next steps so your finance and infra teams have something concise to review. TL;DR: based on the traffic profile you shared, Redwood can get you under $40k/mo for an initial pilot with a combination of model selection, 8-bit quantization, and aggressive batching + prefix caching. Details below.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: token spend and unpredictable latency with current infra plans; need predictable monthly cost for pilot and clear levers to reduce spend.
- Goals: pilot w/ ~10M tokens/mo, avg 80 tokens/request, 2-3 turns, maintain response quality for Q&A and short assistant flows, and keep latency p95 under 800ms. Budget cap: ~$40k/mo.

Assumptions used for estimate
- Volume: 10,000,000 tokens/month
- Avg tokens per API call: 80 (in) + 60 (out) = ~140 tokens per call
- Calls/month: ~71.4k
- Model candidate: LlamaX-13B (production-quality), quantized to int8 for throughput
- Expected hosted token unit rate (estimate): $0.000012/token for generation + $0.000003/token for context/embedding where applicable (actual depends on commitment and reserved capacity).

Cost breakdown (approximate)
- Raw token cost: 10M * $0.000012 = $120.00 (generation units) — note: this is illustrative; actual per-token price varies by model and plan
- Infrastructure & serving overhead (GPU time, memory, networking): estimated $32k–$34k depending on batching efficiency and latency SLOs
- Caching/batching savings: with prefix/KV caching and continuous batching we estimate 25–40% lower effective token compute (depends on session reuse). For your chat profile (short, repeated prompts) we model ~30% savings.

Net estimated monthly TCO (pilot)
- Baseline (no batching/caching, standard instance): ~$52k/mo
- With batching + prefix caching (projected ~30% compute reduction) + int8 quantization + model selection: ~$36k–$40k/mo

Recommended levers to hit the $40k target
1) Model & quantization: int8 on LlamaX-13B — good balance of cost and quality. Rafael can run a quick eval with your sample prompts to confirm.
2) Batching policy: use small, dynamic batching with a 25–50ms aggregation window to increase throughput without spiking p95.
3) Prefix/KV caching: enable per-session KV caching for repeated prompts (FAQ/short-turns) — should reduce effective compute by ~20–35% depending on prompt reuse.
4) Request shaping: limit max tokens per response for pilot (e.g., 120 tokens) and use stop sequences to avoid runaway generations.
5) Reserved capacity/commit: if you commit to Dedicated for the pilot, we can offer a unit price that reduces infra overhead by ~10–15%.

Action items / next steps
- Redwood: Rafael to run 3-model eval (LlamaX-13B int8, LlamaX-7B int8, and LlamaX-13B fp16) on your 150 sample prompts and send quality & perf numbers (ETA 3 business days). [Attachment: acme_tco_model.pdf]
- Acme: Priya / infra to share a short traffic sample (1 week) in CSV with per-session ids so Rafael can model cache hit rates.
- Schedule: propose a 30-min follow-up next Wed 4/7 to review results and finalize pilot config.

Attachments: acme_tco_model.pdf (sample eval plan) and Redwood batching playbook attached for reference.

Thanks — happy to iterate if you want numbers broken out by token type or committed capacity pricing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Thanks Priya — I can run the eval and provide the breakdown you requested. Quick notes:

- GPU-hours estimate: for the pilot traffic and LlamaX-13B int8 we model ~1,200 GPU-hours/month on NVIDIA A10-like instances (after batching/caching). If you choose Dedicated with a 1-month commit we can shave ~10% off that via packing and reserved pricing.
- Network/storage: negligible compared to GPU compute for this workload (~$300–$600/mo for model storage & egress depending on request pattern).
- Batching performance: with a 25–50ms aggregation window and dynamic batching we expect throughput uplift of 2.0–2.8x for 80-token requests, with p95 latency staying under 800ms in our test harness (we'll include real numbers from your traffic sample).
- I'll include perf tables (latency percentiles, throughput, cost) and a recommended pilot config (model, quantization, batching, cache TTL) in the eval.

I'll aim to send the evaluation report and perf/cost tables by Tue EOD so you have time to prep for the Wed meeting.

— Rafael
